  How to Submit Public Comment:

  Members of the Public who wish to submit public comment may do so using one of the following
  methods. Public comment is limited to the time allotted.

  In-Person: Complete a Speaker Card, indicating the agenda item number and submit it to the City
  Clerk prior to the meeting. Speakers shall be limited to three (3) minutes per person per item. At the
  Mayor’ s discretion, the time limit may be shortened to allow all speakers to address the City Council.

  Electronic submission of Public Comment is also available via the City’s website as noted below.
  Public Comment submitted electronically will be read into the record. Words that would disrupt the
  meeting, including profanity, obscenity, and discriminatory language, will not be read. Your
  comments must be received by 5:00 P.M. on meeting day.

  Website: Please submit your comments using the online public comment form at Public Comment.

  Watch the Meeting Online

  C. 2021 STATE HOMELAND SECURITY PROGRAM GRANT ACCEPTANCE

  The City of San Gabriel has been awarded grant funds from the 2021 State
  Homeland Security Program (SHSP) for both the San Gabriel Police and Fire
  Departments in the amount of $119,354 and $62,000 respectively. Both public
  safety departments are able to use these funds towards projects from the
  Department of Homeland Security Approved Equipment List and also to
  provide training. Funding for the purchases will be reimbursed through the
  State Homeland Security Program grant. Initial outlay would be $181,354, but
  would be fully reimbursed, with no matching funds. There is no fiscal impact to
  the General Fund.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve the following:

  Police Department
  1. Increase estimated revenue (account 186-3215) and appropriation
  (transfers out) in ‘Other Grants’ Fund by $119,354; and increase
  estimated revenue (transfers in) and appropriation in Capital/Special
  Projects Funds (account 124-751-57-99-380) by $119,354.

  Fire Department

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – May 2, 2023  3
   2. Increase estimated revenue (account 186-3215) and appropriation
  (transfers out) in ‘Other Grants’ Fund by $62,000; and increase estimated
  revenue (transfers in) and appropriation in Capital/Special Projects
  Funds (account 124-761-57-99-380) by $62,000.

  3. Authorize both the Police Chief and Fire Chief to accept the SHSP grant
  and purchase the items under the City’s purchasing policy.

  4. Authorize the City Manager to execute the subrecipient agreement
  between the City and the County of Los Angeles and adopt Resolution
  No. 23-21 amending the Fiscal Year 2022-2023 Operating Budget.

  D. ORDINANCE NO. 688 AMENDING CHAPTER 130 OF THE SAN GABRIEL
  MUNICIPAL CODE, REGARDING GENERAL OFFENSES, TO ALLOW LOCAL
  PROSECUTION OF CERTAIN MISDEMEANORS – SECOND READING AND
  ADOPTION

  Adoption of this Ordinance would modify the San Gabriel Municipal Code to
  add certain misdemeanor crimes that could be prosecuted locally by the City
  Attorney’s office. There is no fiscal impact related to the adoption of this item.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council waive reading and adopt Ordinance No.
  688 entitled “An Ordinance of the City Council of the City of San Gabriel,
  California, Amending Chapter 130 of the San Gabriel Municipal Code,
  Regarding General Offenses.”

  E. ADOPTION OF RESOLUTION NO. 23-27 DECLARING JANUARY 28TH AS
  STAND AGAINST HATE ACTION DAY

  On March 9, 2023, the State of California adopted Senate Conforming
  Resolution 15 (SCR 15) ;declaring January 28th annually as Stand Against Hate
  Action Day. By adopting the proposed resolution, the City of San Gabriel will
  declare January 28th as Stand Against Hate Action Day, calling upon the
  community to collectively denounce hate and celebrate inclusion. There is no
  fiscal impact related to this item.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – May 2, 2023  4
   California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 23-27 declaring
  January 28th annually as Stand Against Hate Action Day.

  F. SECOND AMENDMENT TO AGREEMENT WITH THE SAN GABRIEL VALLEY
  COUNCIL OF GOVERNMENTS (SGVCOG) TO PARTICIPATE IN THE SAN
  GABRIEL VALLEY REGIONAL VEHICLE MILES TRAVELED (VMT) ANALYSIS
  MODEL AND TOOL UPDATE

  The Community Development Department is requesting a second amendment
  to an existing professional services agreement with the San Gabriel Valley
  Council of Government (SGVCOG) to participate in the San Gabriel Valley
  Regional Vehicle Miles Traveled (VMT) Analysis Model and Tool Update at an
  additional cost of $15,000 for a five-year term. San Gabriel is one of 26 cities to
  participate in the regional program to have access to a web-based
  transportation screening tool for development projects for California
  Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) purposes. Funding will be proposed as part
  of the Fiscal Year 2023-2024 budget in account No. 184-800-00-22-000.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve an amendment to an existing
  Memorandum of Agreement (MOA) with the San Gabriel Valley Council of
  Government for an amount not to exceed $15,000.00 for the implementation
  of the San Gabriel Vehicle Miles Traveled (VMT) Analysis Model & Tool Update.

  G. HUMAN, EQUITY, ACCESS AND RELATIONS COMMISSION PROPOSED
  2023 ANNUAL WORKPLAN

  This is the 2023 calendar Annual Work plan developed by the Human Equity,
  Access and Relations Commission for the 2023 calendar year to best fit in
  alignment with the goals and scope of the HEAR Commission as well as the City
  of San Gabriel’s Mission. The workplan includes a request of $2,500 for the
  Mental Wellness Expo in October. Should Council approve the request, this will

   require $2,022.82 from the General Fund and $477.18 remaining funds from the
  San Gabriel Community Foundation Grant received by the City in 2022.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council review and approve the HEAR
  Commission’s Annual Workplan, as presented, for 2023.

  H. ACCEPTANCE OF ASSISTANCE TO FIREFIGHTERS GRANT AWARD AND
  PURCHASE OF WASHER-EXTRACTOR AND DRYER CABINET IN THE
  AMOUNT OF $37,059.77

  The San Gabriel Fire Department has been awarded funds from the 2021
  Assistance to Firefighter Grant (AFG) Program in the amount of $33,690.70. The
  Fire Department is recommending Council’s adoption of Resolution No. 23-24
  and authorization for the City Manager to issue purchase orders for the
  acquisition of a washer-extractor and drying cabinet as detailed in the report.
  This is a United States Homeland Security AFG Program managed by Federal
  Emergency Management Agency. The total outlay would be $37,030.21. The
  grant will pay for $33,663.83 and the general fund is obligated to a matching
  amount of $3,366.38. The deadline to use these funds is August 29, 2024.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council
  1. Adopt Resolution No. 23-24 accepting the grant and appropriation.
  2. Increase the appropriations in the Fire Department special project grant
  account by $33,690.70, account #124-761-57-99-390.
  3. Authorize the City Manager to issue purchase orders for the purchase of
  a washer-extractor and drying cabinet as detailed in the staff report.

   A. SMITH PARK RESOURCE DISCUSSION - PICKLEBALL

  During the July 18, 2022 Community Services Commission meeting, staff
  presented the community’s request to build pickleball courts at Smith Park.
  After much deliberation and public comment provided by the community, the
  Commission recommended that staff present a proposal to the City Council to
  add four new permanent pickleball courts at Smith Park. Staff have researched
  the costs associated with the construction of new courts including laying
  concrete, lighting, fencing with wind screens, walkways, surfacing, and striping
  and have included estimates in this report. Staff propose the use of existing
  Park Impact Fees for the implementation of the new pickleball courts because
  this is a qualifying expansion to the public amenities. The total cost shall not
  exceed $180,000. Council has previously approved $30,000 additional funds
  from the Tennis Special Activities Fund in Fiscal Year 2022-2023 to resurface
  and restripe the existing courts.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council review the proposal to construct four
  new permanent pickleball courts and approve the funding request necessary to
  implement the project.

  B. DISCUSSION ON THE TAXPAYER PROTECTION AND GOVERNMENT
  ACCOUNTABILITY ACT BALLOT INITATIVE – REQUEST FOR DIRECTION ON
  AN OFFICIAL CITY POSITION AND CONSIDERATION OF ADOPTION OF A
  RESOLUTION NO. 23-28 EITHER IN SUPPORT OF OR IN OPPOSITION TO
  THE BALLOT INITIATIVE

  A ballot initiative called the Taxpayer Protection and Government
  Accountability Act was created and sponsored by several taxpayer protection
  groups, and gathered sufficient signatures to qualify for placement on the
  November 2024 election. Staff is seeking direction on an official City position
  on the ballot initiative and consideration of a resolution establishing the City’s
  position on the measure. There is no fiscal impact associated with discussing
  the City’s position on the ballot initiative. The potential financial effects of the
  ballot measure, should it be successful, are difficult to estimate, those in favor
  of the initiative suggest that the initiative will save taxpayers millions of dollars,

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – May 2, 2023  7
   and those opposed to the initiative suggest that the measure will cost cities
  millions of dollars in lost revenue.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council discuss the Taxpayer Protection and
  Government Accountability act and if desired, adopt Resolution No. 23-28
  supporting the Supporting Taxpayer Protection and Government
  Accountability Act.

  C. APPOINTMENTS TO THE CIVIL SERVICE, COMMUNITY SERVICES, DESIGN
  REVIEW, HISTORIC PRESERVATION AND CULTURAL RESOURCE, AND
  PLANNING COMMISSIONS

  On April 26 and 27, 2023, the City Council conducted interviews for the above-
  named Commissions for vacancies with terms ending May 31, 2023. The Council
  is requested to consider appointments to the Commissions for both scheduled
  and unscheduled vacancies, and for a waitlist. There is no fiscal impact related
  to this item.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council appoint Commissioners for scheduled
  and unscheduled vacancies on the Civil Service, Community Services, Design
  Review, Historic Preservation and Cultural Resource, and Planning
  Commissions, and select individuals they would like to add to the waitlist
  should any unscheduled vacancies arise.
